description:
FILED s470bj.  #1140's `escapes` fact treats `map`, `grep`, `sort`, `reverse`
and `values` as ESCAPING their array argument, because all five hand the caller
ALIASES of the source elements -- probed against perl 5.40.3
(`$_++ for reverse @a` increments @a; `$_++ for sort @a` writes back; `map { $_
} @a` aliases `$_`).  That is sound but conservative: a block that only READS
`$_` cannot write anything, and neither can `reverse`/`values` in a position
whose value is copied.

MEASURED COST at filing (the only one found in the four populations): `lib/mro.pm`'s
C3 linearization loses `p-foreach-raw` on `@seqs` in three loops, because line
84 is `@seqs = grep { scalar @$_ } @seqs;` -- a block that only reads.  No
`local-push` site was lost to it in perl-tests/ or lib/.  So this is a filler,
not a target.

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: the oracle already exists and is already used for exactly
this question one level up -- `Pl::VarAnnotator::_text_gate_tags($name, $body,
1)`, the shared per-name gate list #760's `raw-closure-capture` runs over a
closure body.  Run it for `'$_'` (and `'$a'`/`'$b'` for a sort block) over the
BLOCK's source; no gate firing => the block only reads => the argument is a
read, not an escape.  Note the residue that keeps it conservative anyway: the
block can CALL something that writes `$_`, so a body containing any call must
stay an escape (`for (@a) { f() }` where f does `$_ = 1` DOES write @a in perl).

BAR: corpus-diff + the lib A/B (mro.pm is the expected mover, and its three
loops going back to `p-foreach-raw` IS the acceptance), the full sweep (a
name-resolution-shaped change), and a guard row per member of the family --
including the NEGATIVES: a block that writes `$_`, and a block that calls a sub.


=== SIZED s473r (2026-09-07) â NOT a filler: 30.6 % at a site.  PROMOTED, still open. ===

THE TASK UNDER-SIZED ITSELF, and the correction is the finding.  It looked
for lost `local-push` sites and found one cost (lib/mro.pm`s three C3 loops),
concluding "this is a filler, not a target".  It did not look for lost
`p-foreach-raw` RUNS â and that is where the cost is, because #1409 (round 30)
made a SINGLE bare array take the `:arrays t` run and #1140`s escape verdict
is what licenses it.

THE MEASUREMENT (ab-lisp.pl: two .lisp files, ONE core, interleaved,
best-of-5, byte-identical but for one form; box load 1.3):

    my @a = (1..1000); my $s=0;
    my $c = grep { $_ > 0 } @a;                 # <- READ-ONLY block, once
    for (1..30000) { for my $x (@a) { $s += $x } }

    with the grep:     (p-foreach ($x @a) :my t â¦)                    0.2872 s
    without it:        (p-foreach-raw ($x (vector @a)) :arrays t â¦)   0.1992 s
                                                                      -30.6 %

ONE read-only `grep` ANYWHERE IN THE FILE costs the array its raw run at
EVERY foreach over it â the escape verdict is per-name and region-wide.  That
is 30.6 % of a read loop, well above the 20 %-of-a-row bar, and the shape
(`my $n = grep {â¦} @a` beside a `for (@a)`) is ordinary perl.

THE FIX IS STILL THE ONE THIS TASK DESCRIBES, and the sort precedent is the
model to copy exactly (rule 11):
  * `_tw_walk_funcall_args` already special-cases `sort` with a block: it
    records the escape under its OWN reason (`sort-block`) and sets
    `$arr_read = 1` so the position-blind leaf reason is not added as well.
    `map`/`grep` need the same, under a reason of their own (`topic-block`).
  * `_array_verdicts` then relaxes that reason.  For `sort` the test is
    REGION-WIDE (`_name_touched($ctx,"$a")` / `$b`); for `$_` region-wide
    cannot work â every `for (@x)` in the region touches `$_`.  So the test
    must be PER BLOCK: `_text_gate_tags("$_", <the block`s source>, 1)`, with
    no gate firing meaning the block only reads.
  * THE RESIDUE THE TASK NAMES IS LOAD-BEARING: a block that CALLS anything
    must stay an escape, because a callee can write the global `$_`
    (`for (@a) { f() }` where f does `$_ = 1` DOES write @a in perl).  So the
    licence is "no gate fires AND the block body contains no call".
  * The one piece of machinery that is NOT already there: getting the BLOCK`s
    SOURCE TEXT at the point of decision.  `_tw_walk_funcall_args` has the
    OpcodeTree node, not a PPI element; `_arr_mark_subtree` walks the subtree
    and is the place to look for how to reach the text (or to collect the
    leaf contents).  Size that first â it is the only unknown in the design.

BAR: it is a VarAnnotator change, so the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table makes the FULL
SWEEP the gate; plus corpus-diff with every differing file explained by shape
(lib/mro.pm`s three loops regaining `p-foreach-raw` IS the acceptance the task
names), emission-ab over the wide list with RCDIFF 0, the generation bump and
the three artifacts (cl/pcl-mro.lisp MUST change), and guard rows for the
NEGATIVES probed vs perl 5.40.3: `$_++ for grep {â¦} @a` writes back,
`map { $_ = 1 } @a` writes back, `grep { f() } @a` where f writes `$_` writes
back â all three must stay ESCAPING.

s473r sized it and did not take it: two runtime levers had already shipped in
the round and this one is an emission change in the fact machinery.
subject: A map/grep/sort BLOCK that only reads $_ (or $a/$b) does not alias-escape its source array â refine #1140 escapes
